sites.name: M/V HONDIUS
sites.country: TENERIFE / CANARY ISLANDS — EVACUATION IN PROGRESS
sites.desc: Evacuation actively underway as of 10 May morning: passengers disembarking in groups of 5 via Zodiac boats, transferred in sealed buses to Tenerife Sur airport. No suspected cases remaining aboard per Euronews/WHO. Spain health inspectors boarded pre-disembarkation — no rodents found on vessel. Skeleton crew of 30 to sail Hondius to Rotterdam for full decontamination; German woman's body still aboard. Luggage remains on ship and will be returned to passengers separately.

sites.name: USHUAIA / ARGENTINA ROUTE
sites.desc: Working hypothesis (WHO/NBC): index case (Dutch male, died 11 Apr) likely infected during birdwatching outing near Ushuaia landfill before boarding 01 Apr. Argentine Malbrán Institute conducting rodent trapping along travel route; Argentina tally 101 hantavirus infections since Jun 2025 — roughly double prior-year period. Index case returned from Uruguay to Argentina only 4 days before boarding.

sites.name: SAINT HELENA
sites.desc: 30 passengers disembarked 24 Apr including Dutch index male's body and Dutch widow (later died Johannesburg) and Swiss confirmed male. UKHSA contact-tracing 30 disembarkees plus 82 pax and 6 crew from 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight. Four Tristan da Cunha islanders also rode Hondius to St Helena per UK minister Doughty. Disembarkees from 12+ countries dispersed globally before hantavirus confirmed 02 May.

sites.name: JOHANNESBURG
sites.desc: Case 2 (Dutch widow, PCR+) died Johannesburg hospital 26 Apr — confirmed Andes virus fatality. Case 3 (British guide Martin Anstee, 56, PCR+) treated at Johannesburg ICU; condition improved and transferred to Netherlands. A second British national in a South Africa health facility confirmed PCR-positive 08 May. NICD contact-traced 65+ contacts from 25 Apr Airlink flight.

sites.name: AMSTERDAM / NIJMEGEN
sites.desc: British Case 3 (Anstee, 56) transferred to Netherlands after improving in South Africa. Dutch crew member (41, confirmed) treated at Radboud UMC Nijmegen. Netherlands lab PCR-confirmed German woman died of Andes virus. Three patients medevacked from Cape Verde to Schiphol 06 May; specialist teams received in hazmat suits. KLM flight attendant PCR-NEGATIVE confirmed by WHO. Netherlands sending two repatriation planes (Sunday + Monday sweeper). Ship to proceed to Rotterdam post-Tenerife for full disinfection.

sites.name: LONDON
sites.desc: UKHSA confirmed 2 British nationals PCR+ (one transferred to Netherlands, one confirmed 08 May in South Africa health facility) and one probable/suspected case on Tristan da Cunha (08 May). UK repatriation flight from Tenerife scheduled mid-Sunday operation. UKHSA also tracking 4 Tristan da Cunha islanders who rode Hondius to St Helena.

sites.name: PARIS
sites.desc: Eight French nationals identified as close contacts of confirmed case on 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight — none were on the cruise. One reporting mild symptoms, isolated pending PCR. French repatriation flight from Tenerife confirmed for Sunday 10 May operation.

sites.name: ZURICH
sites.desc: PCR-confirmed male passenger disembarked St Helena 24 Apr via South Africa and Qatar; symptoms onset 01 May, tested positive Andes virus 05 May at University Hospital Zurich. Swiss confirmation 06 May. Wife (also on trip) asymptomatic and isolating; Swiss contact tracing ongoing.

sites.name: BERLIN / DÜSSELDORF
sites.desc: German woman died on board 02 May (fever/malaise onset 28 Apr, pneumonia). Netherlands postmortem PCR confirmed Andes virus. Asymptomatic 65-year-old German contact evacuated 06 May, returned Düsseldorf, tested NEGATIVE. RKI contact tracing active. German nationals repatriating via Netherlands flight from Tenerife (Sunday operation).

sites.name: ALICANTE
sites.desc: CLEARED (FIRST PCR): Centro Nacional de Microbiología confirmed first PCR NEGATIVE for the 32-year-old woman hospitalized in negative-pressure isolation — seated two rows behind deceased Dutch woman on 25 Apr Airlink flight. Second confirmatory PCR required per protocol; if also negative, patient transfers to Gómez Ulla Military Hospital Madrid. Status remains monitor pending second PCR result.

sites.name: TENERIFE
sites.desc: Hondius arrived Granadilla ~05:30 local 10 May; disembarkation commenced ~08:00. Spanish Health Minister Garcia on site; 358 Guardia Civil agents involved. Spanish inspectors boarded ship pre-disembarkation — confirmed no rodents found. Canary Islands president Clavijo receiving vessel under WHO/Spain IHR agreement; authorities want ship and all passengers departed by end of 10 May.

sites.name: MADRID
sites.desc: Gómez Ulla Military Hospital activated to receive 14 Spanish Hondius passengers (13 pax + 1 crew per Oceanwide manifest). Spanish nationals first to disembark; transferred by sealed army buses to Tenerife Sur airport, flown Madrid for military hospital quarantine. PCR on arrival + Day 7; twice-daily temperature monitoring; individual rooms, no visitors. Alicante woman to transfer here if second PCR negative.

sites.name: BARCELONA
sites.desc: Two Barcelona contacts monitored: (1) South African woman (asymptomatic flight contact of Dutch deceased) spent ~1 week here before returning to South Africa — confirmed asymptomatic. (2) Barcelona-resident woman identified 09 May as flight contact after mid-flight seat change; asymptomatic, placed under official monitoring per Spanish Health Ministry.

sites.name: TRISTAN DA CUNHA
sites.desc: UKHSA confirmed probable case 08 May: British male islander aboard Hondius during 13–15 Apr Tristan da Cunha stop; symptoms onset 28 Apr, stable in isolation on island. UK Minister Doughty confirmed patient is 'an islander'; spouse isolating. Four additional islanders rode Hondius to St Helena, expanding contact tracing scope.

sites.name: SINGAPORE
sites.desc: CLEARED 09 May: Both male residents (aged 67 and 65) tested NEGATIVE for hantavirus including Andes virus via multiple PCR samples — Singapore CDA confirmed. Both had disembarked Hondius at St Helena and traveled on 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight. Monitoring continues through full incubation window.

sites.name: ONTARIO
sites.desc: Two Ontario residents self-isolating — Hondius passengers who returned home early, asymptomatic. Canadian nationals aboard to be repatriated via dedicated flight from Tenerife. PHAC coordinating monitoring per 07 May government statement.

sites.name: QUEBEC
sites.desc: One Quebec resident self-isolating — not a Hondius passenger but shared homebound flight with two Canadian Hondius disembarkees. Asymptomatic; PHAC monitoring active.

sites.name: ARIZONA
sites.desc: ADHS monitoring one returning passenger under 42-day observation. Asymptomatic as of 10 May. CDC notified ADHS 05 May; public risk assessed as very low. Part of domestic US monitoring cohort across 6 states.

sites.name: CALIFORNIA
sites.desc: CDPH monitoring one returned Hondius traveler via daily temperature checks and symptom assessment. A second California resident remains aboard ship and will transit Tenerife to Nebraska NQU via CDC/HHS biocontainment charter. No California residents reported ill or infected as of 10 May.

sites.name: GEORGIA
sites.desc: Georgia DPH monitoring two residents who returned from Hondius. Both in good health with no signs of infection as of 10 May. Following CDC recommendations. Part of domestic US monitoring cohort across 6 states.

sites.name: TEXAS
sites.desc: Texas DSHS monitoring two returning Hondius passengers. Both asymptomatic as of 10 May. Part of domestic US monitoring cohort across 6 states.

sites.name: VIRGINIA
sites.desc: VDH monitoring one returning Hondius passenger. Asymptomatic. CDC classified response as Level-3; Emergency Operations Center activated. Six states — AZ, CA, GA, TX, VA, NJ — monitoring at least 9 early-disembarkees or contacts.

sites.name: NEW JERSEY
sites.desc: NJ DOH monitoring two individuals potentially exposed to a Hondius passenger post-disembarkation during air travel. Neither symptomatic as of 10 May. NJ DOH confirmed exposure occurred during air travel abroad; residents were not Hondius passengers themselves.

sites.name: NEBRASKA
sites.desc: Nebraska Medicine / UNMC National Quarantine Unit (NQU) activated for 17–19 Americans inbound from Tenerife via Offutt AFB. CDC confirmed: NO mandatory quarantine; passengers evaluated at NQU then may opt for 42-day home self-monitoring with daily contact with state/local health departments. NQU has 20 negative-airflow individual rooms. Medical director Dr. Wadman confirmed teams prepared.

sites.name: UTAH
sites.desc: Utah DHHS confirmed at least one Utah resident among the 17 Americans aboard MV Hondius. Person is asymptomatic and disembarking Tenerife with federal escort to Nebraska NQU for evaluation. No Utah residents monitored at home as of 10 May.

sites.name: MANILA
sites.desc: 38 Filipino crew members aboard Hondius; Philippines DOH confirmed none currently ill as of 10 May. Skeleton crew of ~30 will remain aboard to sail vessel to Rotterdam; most crew repatriated from Tenerife. Monitoring continues through incubation window.

sites.name: DUBLIN
sites.desc: Two Irish nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per ECDC briefing. Repatriation flight from Tenerife confirmed via dedicated national or EU Civil Protection Mechanism aircraft. Irish Dept of Health coordinating with ECDC and WHO; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: PRAIA
sites.desc: Hondius anchored off Praia 03–06 May; departed 19:15 local 06 May for Tenerife. Three medevac patients evacuated here 06 May — two flew to Amsterdam (received by hazmat-suited teams at Schiphol), third plane made unscheduled refueling stop at Gran Canaria after Morocco refused permission and a medical equipment malfunction caused delays. Cape Verde unable to handle full passenger evacuation.

sites.name: COPENHAGEN
sites.desc: Danish Patient Safety Authority confirmed one Danish national was aboard MV Hondius. Person returned to Denmark end of April, self-isolating, no symptoms, not in close contact with any confirmed case. Monitoring active per national protocol.

sites.name: BRUSSELS
sites.desc: Belgian nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per ECDC briefing. Repatriation from Tenerife via Netherlands flight (Sunday operation) per Spain Health Minister Garcia. Belgian federal health authorities coordinating with ECDC. No symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: WELLINGTON
sites.desc: NZ confirmed among 12+ countries monitoring Hondius nationals. At least one NZ national still aboard ship awaiting Monday final repatriation flight (6 pax from Australia, NZ and Asian countries). NZ Ministry of Health coordinating contact tracing; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: STOCKHOLM
sites.desc: Sweden confirmed among 12+ countries monitoring Hondius nationals who disembarked. Swedish Public Health Agency (Folkhälsomyndigheten) coordinating; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: ANKARA
sites.desc: Turkish nationals aboard Hondius to be repatriated via dedicated flight from Tenerife (Sunday operation per Spain Health Minister Garcia). Turkish Ministry of Health coordinating; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: BASSETERRE
sites.desc: Saint Kitts and Nevis confirmed among 12+ countries monitoring nationals who disembarked MV Hondius. Local health authorities monitoring; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: ATHENS
sites.desc: Greek nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per ECDC briefing and Spain Health Minister Garcia (Greeks to depart on Netherlands flight). Greek Ministry of Health coordinating with ECDC; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: WARSAW
sites.desc: Polish nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per ECDC briefing. Polish Chief Sanitary Inspectorate coordinating with ECDC; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: LISBON
sites.desc: Portuguese nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per ECDC briefing. DGS Portugal coordinating with ECDC; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: SYDNEY / CANBERRA
sites.desc: At least one Australian national disembarked at Saint Helena 24 Apr and reportedly returned home. Additional Australian nationals remain aboard Hondius; Spain Health Minister Garcia confirmed a final Monday flight will evacuate ~6 passengers from Australia, New Zealand and Asian countries. Australian health authorities monitoring; no symptomatic cases reported.
